selectedCompleteRows.text: | [Core needle biopsy: a small piece of tissue architecture](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/specimens/core-needle-biopsy) | Three panels show a narrow sampled strip within an uneven tissue target, the matching tissue core enlarged with neighboring cells still together, and the examined window beside regions outside it that the core does not represent. | `core-is-a-local-window-v1-light.svg` | Present | Present |

| [Fixed, fresh-frozen and viable tissue: different kinds of input](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/specimens/ffpe-vs-fresh-frozen-vs-viable) | Three aligned preparation scenes show a fixed wax block and thin section, a snap-frozen tissue piece with a molecular-analysis symbol, and a viable cell aliquot beside a recovery and identity check. Fixed material preserves architecture but cannot recover original living cells; frozen material preserves analytes without guaranteeing viability; viable material needs workflow-specific recovery and function checks. There is no universal best preparation. | `fixed-frozen-viable-preserved-properties-b10-v1-light.svg` | Present | Present |

| [Fine needle aspiration: learning from collected cells](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/specimens/fine-needle-aspiration) | Two schematic panels compare neighboring cells in a continuous core with a vessel containing fluid, individual cells, a cell cluster and a small tissue fragment; an optional preparation arrow leads from the recovered material to a cell block that does not reconstruct its original locations. | `core-versus-recovered-material-v2-light.svg` | Present | Present |

| [RNA integrity](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/specimens/rna-integrity) | A schematic RNA electropherogram highlights early RNA and ribosomal features for a method-defined integrity score, beside a separate equal-width length distribution with 60 percent of selected signal area above 200 nucleotides and a fragmented transcript illustration. | `rna-trace-score-and-length-fraction-v2-light.svg` | Present | Present |

| [Surgical resection specimen: a tissue map with boundaries](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/specimens/surgical-resection-specimen) | A fictional oriented specimen has keyed superior and lateral outer surfaces, a selected central region A and surface region B, and visible unselected space. Each selected region connects to its own labeled tissue block. A fictional test result is attached only to block A, while block B and unselected tissue remain outside that result. The local ink key is invented and no margin-clearance claim is made. | `oriented-specimen-to-selected-blocks-b10-v1-light.svg` | Present | Present |

| [Tissue is non-renewable: planning a finite specimen budget](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/specimens/tissue-is-non-renewable) | A finite tissue block becomes a smaller remaining block as sections are allocated to slides and extraction. One-way arrows carry physical material into those uses; stored slides can remain, while extraction changes the material and loses its original architecture. A separate digital dataset branches into two copies with no reverse arrow to the original block. No universal section thickness, test count or allocation is prescribed. | `finite-tissue-use-and-reusable-data-b10-v1-light.svg` | Present | Present |

| [Vacuum-assisted biopsy: collecting several tissue pieces](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/specimens/vacuum-assisted-biopsy) | One panel links three selected schematic tissue locations to three separate vacuum-collected pieces; another shows an oriented removed specimen with a documented direction key, an inked outer surface and one mapped section, without a negative-margin or clearance label. | `sampled-pieces-versus-oriented-boundary-v2-light.svg` | Present | Present |
